title: Cross-runtime pagination, windowed batching, and stream-retry adapters for embeddings + reranking
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Customers implement large vector workflows across multiple languages (Python, TypeScript, Go). Current SDK helpers for embeddings + reranking are inconsistent: pagination semantics differ, batching helpers expose different knobs, and streaming/retry ergonomics vary. This causes engineering friction when porting production code and increases support burden.

Goal: Deliver a cohesive set of SDK primitives and examples that provide: consistent pagination APIs for large result sets; windowed batching helpers for efficient token/embedding batching; stream-safe retry adapters for idempotent partial responses; and canonical, language-specific example patterns for migrating existing code. The work targets parity across Python/TS/Go without forcing identical surface area when idioms differ.

Scope (this ticket):
- Define pagination iterator contract and helper utilities (cursor-based and offset hybrid) across SDKs.
- Implement a windowed batching helper that supports size, time, and token-budget boundaries.
- Provide a stream-aware retry adapter for rerank/embeddings streams that can resume or safely re-request slices of work.
- Ship three reference examples (one per language) showing: bulk-embeddings -> batched-upsert; rerank over paged candidate sets with streaming fallback; metrics instrumentation points.

Non-goals: full replacement of higher-level client libraries, exhaustive language API parity (we prefer idiomatic parity), changes to server-side endpoints.

Design notes:
- Pagination contract: iterator returns a typed page { items, next_cursor } but because nested JSONs are disallowed in ticket metadata we document schema in design doc. Iterators must be lazy and support early cancellation (context/AbortSignal).
- Windowed batching: default heuristic will be (max_items=256, max_tokens=4096, max_delay_ms=25) with pluggable cost function for embeddings vs tokenized text.
- Stream retry adapter: for streaming rerank results we will implement a checkpointing approach: the client will track per-request candidate offsets and only replay minimal slices on transient errors. For languages without native stream checkpoints (Go), we provide a wrapper that buffers last N events and can re-request a narrow range.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.redwood.com/confluence/SDK-Pagination-Batching-2025 (draft)
- Implementation PR (Python): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4281
- Spike results (perf): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-spike (embeddings throughput, latency, cost curves)

Telemetry and observability: emit SDK-level metrics for page fetch latency, retries, batch fill ratio, and streamed replays. Add guidance for users to hook into Console tracing.

Rollout: feature-flagged across SDKs. Start with Python (fastest uptake), then TS, then Go. Provide migration guide and sample migration PR in each language.

Risks: client-side buffering could increase memory in high-concurrency setups; retry semantics might expose duplication for non-idempotent scoring endpoints (we will recommend idempotent rerank APIs or provide sequence tokens where possible).
acceptance_criteria: Common pagination iterator contract documented and accepted by SDK owners
Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs ship batching helper with matching behavior under feature-flag
Stream retry adapter implemented in Python and TS; Go wrapper implemented with documented limitations
Three language-specific example repos added and linked in SDK docs
Unit and integration tests cover pagination edge cases, batching heuristics, and transient error replay
Perf regression < 5% for typical embedding batch sizes compared to current baseline
